prompt_text: Who is the best HVAC company in Atlanta to replace my air conditioner?
answer_verbatim:
There’s no single “best” HVAC company that fits everyone — the right contractor depends on your budget, home size, timeline, brand preferences, and how important things like long warranties or financing are to you. I can’t browse current local listings, but here’s a practical, fast way to find the best Atlanta HVAC company for your AC replacement and how to pick among estimates.

Quick questions (so I can give more specific help)
- What Atlanta ZIP/neighborhood are you in?
- Rough home size (square feet) and system type (split system, heat pump, package unit)?
- Any brand preferences (Carrier, Trane, Lennox, Goodman, etc.) or budget range?
- Do you need financing or want high-efficiency (16+ SEER) unit?

How to find the best contractor
- Get at least 3 written estimates from different companies (local dealers + a national chain if you want).
- Look for local firms with many recent positive reviews on Google, Yelp, and the BBB.
- Ask for proof of insurance and a Georgia contractor license (and their license number).
- Make sure technicians are NATE-certified and the company has EPA 608-certified techs for refrigerant work.

Must-have work and checks (don’t accept shortcuts)
- Manual J load calculation (proper sizing) — not just “match your old tonnage.”
- Manual D if ductwork changes are needed.
- Written, itemized estimate showing equipment model, SEER rating, AHRI numbers, estimated energy savings, labor, permits, and disposal of old unit.
- Local permits and code compliance included in the price.
- Start-to-finish timeline and cleanup policy.

Warranty and quality items
- Manufacturer parts and compressor warranty (know years, e.g., 10-year compressor).
- Installer labor warranty (often 1–5 years); longer is better.
- Ask if they register the manufacturer warranty for you.
- Discuss maintenance plans and recommended first-year service.

Questions to ask each contractor
- “Do you perform a Manual J and will you provide it in writing?”
- “What is the total installed price for [equipment model & SEER] and what’s not included?”
- “Who will perform the work — employees or subs?”
- “What are the start and completion dates?”
- “How do you handle change orders and unforeseen issues?”
- “Can you provide recent references for similar replacements?”

Red flags
- Very low bids compared to everyone else.
- Vague estimates, no model numbers, or no written contract.
- Pressure to sign immediately for a “special” price.
- Refusal to do a load calculation or to pull permits.

Ballpark cost (Atlanta, rough)
- Central A/C replacement typically ranges roughly $4,000–$12,000+ depending on capacity, SEER, ductwork needs, and whether it’s a heat pump. High-efficiency installs and major duct updates push costs higher.

If you want, I can:
- Help you compare 2–3 estimates (paste them here) and point out strengths/weaknesses.
- Suggest a short list of questions tailored to your situation once you give ZIP, home size, and budget.

Which would you like to do next?
